title: Improve INT8/FP8 quantized matmul kernels and smoothquant+dequant fusion for throughput and latency
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Performance: Faster INT8/FP8 matmul kernels and fused smoothquant+dequant paths; no accuracy regressions observed. Rollout: incremental canary followed by global rollout.
description:
Motivation: Quantized inference (INT8/FP8) is a major cost lever for customers. Our previous kernels left optimization headroom for fused dequantization and smoothquant scale handling which causes extra memory traffic and suboptimal batching behavior. This PR implements a set of kernel and scheduler changes to reduce memory bandwidth, improve throughput for large-batch tail workloads, and reduce p99 latency for single-request flows while preserving model quality.

What I changed (high level):
- Implement fused GEMM + dequantization + smoothquant scaling path for INT8 and FP8 inputs where hardware supports vectorized dequant. This avoids explicit dequant buffers in hot paths.
- Add an alternate execution path for models using SmoothQuant-like per-channel scales: compute scale factors on-the-fly during packing and apply them inside the matmul kernel to remove an extra element-wise multiply pass.
- Improve INT8/FP8 kernel microkernel tiling and register blocking to better utilize AVX-512/AMX when available. Added fast-path for 2x K-block sizes common in our transformer workloads.
- Scheduler changes: heuristic to prefer fused-kernel nodes in continuous batching planner when estimated memory pressure is low; fall back to safe dequant path otherwise. This reduces wasted copy/dequant steps in batching.
- KV cache interaction: avoid temporarily materializing dequantized KV pages for cached segments by supporting a cached-quantized-kv view and a lazy dequantization hook in the runtime. This reduces peak memory and improves throughput for long-context streaming requests.
- Tests & perf harness: extended perf-canary to run INT8/FP8 microbenchmarks across representative seq-lens (32/256/1024) and batch sizes; added unit tests validating numerical equivalence within tolerance.

Performance summary (perf-canary aggregate):
- FP8: up to 1.8x throughput improvement on A100 when using fused path, average 1.5x for batch sizes 8-32 for seq=1024.
- INT8: 1.2-1.4x throughput improvement on x86 AVX-512; p99 latency reduced ~15% on small batches (batch=1-4).
- Memory: peak working set reduced ~20% on long-context generation because we avoid materializing dequant KV buffers.
- Model quality: end-to-end logprob/accuracy difference within 0.1% for evaluated T5 and LLaMA checkpoints with SmoothQuant enabled.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Runtime feature gate: quant_fused_kernels (defaults to on for supported hardware). A runtime flag and per-model compatibility check allow safe rollbacks.
- For hardware without FP8/INT8 vector dequant support, runtime falls back to the older dequant path transparently.
- Canary rollout plan: start with internal perf-canary clusters, then small percentage of hosted traffic for customers opted-in to experimental performance, then full rollout after metrics and error budgets are stable.

Testing notes:
- Fixed a flaky quantized-tests job by improving random seed management in the quant kernel tests and increasing tolerance for edge-case denormals on older CPUs.
- Added deterministic golden outputs for a small set of heads to catch regressions in the fused path.

Risks and mitigations:
- Numerical differences: covered with unit tests and model evals; feature gate allows quick disable.
- Scheduling regressions: the scheduler heuristics are conservative and only prefer fused paths when estimated memory remains under threshold; added telemetry to monitor selection ratios.

Related: ENG-4123 (quant kernel perf epic), perf-canary runs referenced in PR comments, SUP-7124 customer incident that motivated KV cache materialization fix.
